results.resolution: No ops. Ninth pass, new sources only. None of them gives a second independent account of the 1986 one-pitch 5.6 Southeast Face. It still rests on the guidebook alone, and the peak page that repeats it copies the guidebook. Owner options are unchanged: (A) merge or delete this row as a duplicate of the sibling wa_witches_tower_south_face standard route; (B) re-point it to the Southeast Face on the guidebook alone; (C) leave it.
results.summary: No second source for the Witches Tower Southeast Face 5.6 turned up in any of the new places searched (climbing journal archive, club and hiking magazines, peak logs, archived pages), so the row stays as it is for the owner to decide.
results.evidence: Ninth pass, 2026-10-01. Every source below was NEW, meaning not tried in r3, r6, r9, r12, r15, r17 or s3. (1) American Alpine Journal, whole-archive search on the publisher's own archive search (exact phrase, AAJ, all years). 'Witches Tower' returns exactly four notes: Northwest Buttress (AAJ 1977), Northeast Face 1976 (AAJ 1979), North Face Dihedral 30 July 1986 (AAJ 1988), and an unrelated California 'Witch Tower'. 'Kevin Kurtz' and 'Curt Snyder' return nothing. 'Asgard Pass' returns only the 1986 North Face Dihedral and a Dragontail winter ascent. So AAJ 1987, where a 1986 new route would appear, has no Southeast Face. (2) Summit magazine, 1988 and 1989 volumes, in-book search. Each has one page matching "Witch's Tower", and that page also matches Enchantment and Dragontail. Neither page matches Kurtz, Snyder, southeast, 5.6, Asgard or Aasgard. Both volumes are no-preview, so the page itself cannot be read. (3) Signpost for Northwest Trails (1990), in-book search: one page matches 'Witches Tower'; 'southeast' and 'scramble' do not match. Further probes hit the search engine's rate-limit page and were stopped there, not bypassed. (4) SummitPost climbers' log for Witches Tower (archived copy; all 11 entries, 2005-2019). Every entry that names a line is the south side or the scramble route: 1985, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008 (x2), 2009, 2011, 2013 (a ramp from the back), 2016 (an easy scramble from the back) and 2019 (an easy scramble). One 2007 entry wishes to come back for 'one of those routes on the East Face', without naming a route or grade. The 2019 entry's 'rappel slings' were on a descent off Dragontail's east ridge toward the tower's base, not on the tower. That is the likely origin of the row's descent_text claim about slings 'on this line', which is therefore unsupported. (5) SummitPost Enchantments area page (archived 2024): only refers readers to the Witches Tower page. (6) Peakbagger peak page (archived 2022) lists nine trip reports (1975-2021). Only one ascent page is archived (2014): a scramble with an ice axe and 220 ft of gain from the col. The others have no archive copy, and the live site is Cloudflare-gated (not bypassed). (7) Google Books catalogue feed with new spellings ("Witch's Tower", "Witches' Tower", "Witch Tower" with Dragontail, Asgard, Cascades, 'Washington climb', 'white rock', 5.6). It finds only the guidebook (2000), Selected Climbs vol 1, Washington Scrambles, Classic Cascade Climbs, Day Hikes in Washington State (2021), the AAJ volumes, Summit and Signpost. No new climbing text. The Google Books API quota was exhausted. (8) HathiTrust full-text search: Cloudflare challenge, not bypassed. (9) theCrag Enchantments area (it has a Witches Tower sector): 403, with no archive copy. (10) Wayback index of cascadeclimbers.com URLs containing 'witch': only the NW Buttress thread (already read in r6) and the unrelated West Witches Tit thread. (11) WTA 2002 Enchantment Lakes trip report and NWHikers 2009 'Witches Tower via South Route': both 403, with no archive copy. (12) Not relevant or empty: komoot 'Witch Tower' highlights (all European monuments); Steph Abegg (mentions the tower only on a Colchuck Balanced Rock page); a Little Annapurna South Face route page (no mention); Lowell Skoog's alpenglow.org (403, and search finds no Witches Tower page there); the Washington Alpine Club's annual (no online copy found). Result: still one independent source (the guidebook, 2000 p.276) for the Southeast Face 5.6, so it cannot be written. The scramble picture is reinforced: eleven more first-hand log entries all climb the easy south/back-side scramble, which is the sibling row's line. Note for the owner: whichever option is chosen, descent_text's sentence about rappel slings 'on this line' has no support (see (4)).
